Screen Time troubleshooting

App Limits not working on iPhone? Check these settings

A limit can fail for several different reasons. Work through the settings in order so you can fix the actual problem without rebuilding your entire Screen Time setup.

By Hussain TaheriPublished September 3, 20268 minute read

Direct answer: Confirm that App and Website Activity is on, open App Limits and verify the selected apps, amount, and customized days, then review Always Allowed. If the limit is still behaving like a reminder, protect the Screen Time settings with a passcode or recreate the limit. Test with a short allowance before relying on it.

Identify what is actually failing

Match the symptom to the first setting to inspect
What you seeCheck firstWhy it matters
No usage report or limitsApp and Website ActivityTurning it off also turns off App Limits and Screen Time reporting
The wrong app is limitedSelected apps and categoriesA category may include a different set of apps than you expected
The limit works on some daysCustomize DaysEach day can have a different allowance
An app stays availableAlways AllowedAllowed apps remain accessible during restricted periods
The settings are easy to changeScreen Time passcodeA separate passcode can protect the configuration

1. Confirm App and Website Activity is turned on

Open Settings, choose Screen Time, then open App and Website Activity. Apple says that turning off App and Website Activity also turns off reporting, Downtime, App Limits, and Always Allowed.

If you recently disabled this setting, turn it back on and open App Limits again. Confirm that the limit you expect is still listed before testing it.

2. Verify the selected apps

Open Settings, choose Screen Time, then choose App Limits. Select the limit and inspect the apps or categories attached to it.

For an individual app, open its category and select the exact app. When multiple apps or categories share one limit, the allowance applies to the selected group. A separate limit is easier to understand when each app serves a different purpose.

3. Check the amount and customized days

Open the limit and check both the daily allowance and Customize Days. A limit that appears correct for Monday may have a different amount on Saturday.

For testing, temporarily choose a short allowance on the current day. Use the selected app until the allowance ends, then confirm whether the limit appears. Restore your intended amount after the test.

4. Review Always Allowed

Open Screen Time, then choose Always Allowed. Apple describes this list as the apps and contacts that remain available during restricted periods and after limits are reached.

Keep genuine safety, communication, navigation, health, and authentication needs available. Remove a distracting app from Always Allowed only when you are confident it is not essential.

5. Make sure you chose the right Screen Time tool

App Limits control how long selected apps can be used during a day. Downtime controls when most apps become unavailable on a schedule. If the problem happens at a predictable hour rather than after a fixed amount of use, Downtime may match the goal better.

Apple notes that Screen Time restrictions may behave like reminders unless the relevant blocking setting is enabled. Review the options shown in your version of iOS, then test the result before depending on it.

6. Protect the settings with a Screen Time passcode

If the limit appears correctly but is too easy to change, open Screen Time and choose Lock Screen Time Settings. Create a passcode and add Apple Account recovery so you can reset it if necessary.

A passcode should add deliberate friction, not create a dangerous lockout. Preserve access to essential apps and keep the recovery account accurate.

7. Check Share Across Devices

Screen Time can synchronize settings and reports across Apple devices signed in to the same Apple Account. Open Screen Time and review Share Across Devices so you know whether the report and settings are intended for one device or several.

8. Delete and recreate only the affected limit

If the settings look correct but the problem continues, remove only that limit and create it again. Apple’s current instructions say you can delete a limit by opening App Limits, swiping left on the limit, and choosing Delete.

Recreate it with one app and a short allowance first. Once that works, add other apps or a longer schedule. Changing one layer at a time makes the source of the problem easier to identify.

9. Check who controls a family limit

If the limit belongs to a child in Family Sharing, the family organizer should review it from the organizer’s device. A setting on your own Screen Time page is not necessarily the setting applied to the child’s account.

When a focused blocker may fit better

Screen Time is useful for broad daily limits and family controls. A dedicated blocker can be clearer when the problem is a specific habit window.

Twilock provides a free Night window for selected apps. Pro adds a Morning window and Strict Mode. Each window is capped at two hours, so Twilock is designed for unwanted scrolling around sleep rather than all day limits, website blocking, or parental control.

For setup instructions, read how to block apps on iPhone. For a broader plan, read how to limit screen time on iPhone.

Frequently asked questions

Why is my Screen Time limit not working?
First confirm that App and Website Activity is on. Then verify the selected app, allowance, customized days, and Always Allowed list. Recreate only the affected limit if those settings are correct.
Why can I continue after the limit appears?
Some Screen Time configurations behave like reminders. Review the blocking options available in your iOS version and consider protecting the settings with a separate Screen Time passcode.
Why does an App Limit affect several apps?
The selected apps or categories may share one allowance. Open the limit and inspect the selection. Create separate limits when you want each app to have its own amount.
Will turning off App and Website Activity remove App Limits?
Apple says turning off App and Website Activity also turns off reporting, Downtime, App Limits, and Always Allowed.
Does Twilock replace every Screen Time feature?
No. Twilock focuses on Night and Morning blocking windows. Apple Screen Time remains better suited to broad daily allowances, family controls, and content restrictions.
